section_7.3.6_Other_drugs.digoxin: In the DIG trial for patients with HFmrEF in sinus rhythm there was a trend to fewer hospitalizations but no reduction in mortality and a trend to excess cardiovascular deaths; insufficient data to recommend routine use.
section_7.3.6_Other_drugs.ivabradine: There are insufficient data on ivabradine in HFmrEF to draw conclusions.

section_7.3.7_Devices.CRT: Post-hoc analyses of landmark CRT trials suggest possible benefit for patients with LVEF >35%, but trials of CRT specifically for HFmrEF were abandoned due to poor recruitment; insufficient evidence to advise CRT in HFmrEF.
section_7.3.7_Devices.ICD: No substantial trials of ICDs for primary prevention in HFmrEF; older trials suggested no benefit for secondary prevention of ventricular arrhythmias in HFmrEF; insufficient evidence to advise ICD therapy in HFmrEF.
section_7.3.7_Devices.interatrial_shunt_device: Implantation of an interatrial shunt device in patients with LVEF â‰¥40% was found to be safe in a study but requires larger investigation before recommendation in HFpEF or HFmrEF.

content.ARNI_recommendation: Treatment with an ARNI may be considered in patients with HFmrEF (sacubitril/valsartan showed beneficial effects in combined analyses of PARADIGM-HF and PARAGON-HF, especially on hospitalizations for HF).
content.section_8_Title: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)

section_8.1_background.nomenclature_and_cutoffs: Acknowledges historical changes and lack of consensus on optimal LVEF cut-offs. The term 'preserved' originated from the CHARM programme and referred to patients with EF >40% not clearly reduced.
section_8.1_background.current_guideline_cutoffs: Current guidelines designate HFmrEF as LVEF 41â€“49%. This guideline keeps HFpEF nomenclature using an EF cut-off of 50%.
section_8.1_background.EACVI_definition: EACVI defines systolic dysfunction as being <52% for males and <54% for females.
section_8.1_background.measurement_variability: Notes variability of echocardiographic LVEF measurements, imaging modality differences, and controversies about precise LVEF cut-offs; cut-offs are arbitrary and may vary with sex, age, and ethnicity.
